source_says.explanation: Section 3.2 and Table 1 establish 230 participants, including 110 people in 55 peer dyads, and Section 3.1 says none were excluded. However, Table 3 uses F (2, 172), implying 175 observations (172 residual degrees of freedom + 3 groups), while the within-arm tests imply 60, 60, and 55 observations (t degrees of freedom + 1). The source does not explain whether the peer observations represent both members jointly or person A alone, nor how the individually completed baseline was reduced to 55 peer-arm observations. Thus 230 and 110 are established participation counts but are not explicitly established people counts for the creativity analyses. The form acknowledges this ambiguity in its exclusions text while retaining definite analyzed-person values. The 175 observations must not simply be relabeled as 175 people, and the difference must not be called 55 exclusions.

source_says.explanation: A uniform participant unit is not explicitly supported for the peer arm. Each dyad had a leader and a supportive member who completed no work independently; all three creativity outcomes use 55 peer observations rather than 110 individual observations. If those are joint dyad solutions, the codebook unit is team; if only person A's outcomes enter, participant can apply but the analyzed-person count for that arm is 55. The available source does not resolve these alternatives. The form's narrative caveat does not establish the categorical participant unit.

source_says.explanation: The local c471 PDF's experimental arm exactly matches c089's 60-person ChatGPT arm on all listed demographic descriptors: age mean 19.20 and SD 1.36; male/female 39/21; sciences/liberal arts/engineering 16/16/28; and prior ChatGPT experience never/seldom/sometimes/often/always 2/10/24/23/1. Both papers use the same baseline and four mathematical creativity tasks. These matches create a concrete possible shared-sample issue that the blank overlap field and generic note about a separate AJET paper do not capture. Neither full text explicitly confirms reuse or independence, and the creativity outcome summaries differ, so shared participants cannot be asserted or counted. Record possible overlap with c471 pending clarification rather than treating the samples as verified independent.

confirmed.statement: The methods explicitly describe individual assignment by lottery to the three conditions, despite the quasi-experimental title.

The reported assigned groups contain 60 ChatGPT users, 60 Google users, and 110 peer-arm people in 55 dyads, totaling 230 people. Table 1 gender and major counts independently sum to these arm totals.

summary: The analyzed-person totals and participant-only outcome units are not fully supported because the peer arm has 55 observations with unresolved representation of its 110 members; identical ChatGPT-arm demographics also raise possible overlap with c471. Eligibility holds because the same lottery-assigned study analyzed 60 ChatGPT and 60 Google participants, already exceeding 50 people.
